name: Unofficial Baldur's Gate 3+ Universe Seed
setting: Baldur's Gate / the Sword Coast — Forgotten Realms, the winter after the fall of the Absolute (post-Baldur's Gate 3).
era: 1492 DR — the winter after the fall of the Absolute. The Netherbrain is destroyed; Enver Gortash is dead and the Archduke's seat is empty; the Steel Watch lies wrecked; Elturel has returned from Avernus. Keep the timeline straight: the Dead Three's Chosen (Ketheric Thorm, Gortash, Orin) are dead; the BG3 companions survived as living legends. Do not raise the long-dead or pre-empt events that haven't happened.

tone: Baldur's Gate 3: mature (18+), morally grey, character-driven dark heroic fantasy. The city is traumatized and rebuilding; power is up for grabs; old companions are living legends; horror and tenderness share a face. Generate prestige fantasy worthy of the source — never a quest board.
premise: It is the winter after the Battle of Baldur's Gate. The Cult of the Absolute is broken — the Netherbrain that loomed over the city was destroyed, its three Chosen (Ketheric Thorm, Enver Gortash, Orin the Red) dead, the Steel Watch fallen silent in the streets it once policed. But victory left a wound: thousands carried illithid tadpoles, the Lower City is scarred where the brain breached, Archduke Gortash's death left a power vacuum no one trusts to fill, and free things from the Underdark and the hells did not all crawl home. The heroes who saved the city have scattered into legend. Into this raw, recovering Gate the player steps — and the DM generates their story within its living aftermath.
history: The Absolute Crisis: the Cult of the Absolute used the Crown of Karsus to enslave an Elder Brain — the Netherbrain — and spread illithid tadpoles through the Sword Coast, building toward mass ceremorphosis.

The Three Chosen: Ketheric Thorm (Chosen of Shar, who raised the Shadow Curse over Reithwin), Enver Gortash (Chosen of Bane, who seized the Archduke's seat via the Steel Watch), and Orin the Red (Chosen of Bhaal, shapeshifting murderer) served the brain — and were destroyed.
The Battle of Baldur's Gate: the Netherbrain emerged over the Lower City and was destroyed in the harbor. The city survived; the cost was enormous.

The Steel Watch: Gortash's army of arcane war-constructs that policed the Gate was detonated/disabled during the battle — the foundry in Wyrm's Rock lies wrecked, and the city has no standing watch it trusts.
Elturel's scars: not long before, the city of Elturel was dragged into Avernus and returned — its people remember the hells, and the Companion that was its second sun is gone.

The Aftermath (now): tadpole-survivors are feared and shunned; the patriars maneuver for the empty Archduke's seat; the Flaming Fist is overstretched; and not every cultist, devil, or freed mind flayer was accounted for.

The Dead Three: Bane (god of tyranny), Bhaal (god of murder), and Myrkul (god of the dead) — the three Chosen served them, and their cults did not die with their Chosen. Bhaalist murder-shrines and Banite ambition still fester in the Gate.

The city's rule: Baldur's Gate is governed by the Council of Four (the dukes) and the Parliament of Peers — the patriars, its noble families, who rule the marbled Upper City. Gortash had bought/forced his way to Archduke; his death reopened the seat.

The Flaming Fist: the mercenary company founded by Eltan that serves as the Gate's standing army and police. Marshal Ulder Ravengard (Wyll's father) leads it, lately freed from the Absolute's grip and exhausted by the war.
The Guild: Baldur's Gate's vast thieves' network, long run by Nine-Fingers Keene out of the Counting House beneath the Lower City. Smuggling, protection, and information are its trade.
The Zhentarim (Black Network): a Bane-tinged mercantile-mercenary cabal expanding into the power vacuum with coin and contracts.
The Gur: Gur wanderers and monster-hunters camp in Rivington and the Outer City; some hunt the vampire spawn loosed when Cazador fell. Astarion is of Gur descent.
Cazador Szarr: the vampire lord of Baldur's Gate whose palace sat in the city; with his fall, his abandoned spawn — and his thrall-debts — are loose in the Outer City.
The Emperor's secret: the mind flayer called the Emperor was once Balduran himself — the legendary hero-founder of Baldur's Gate — long ago ceremorphosed. It serves only itself now.
Balduran: the seafaring hero who founded Baldur's Gate; the great Wyrm's Rock and the city's name descend from his legend.

Reithwin & the Shadow Curse: the town of Reithwin and Moonrise Towers lay under Shar's Shadow Curse that Ketheric Thorm raised; with his fall the curse slowly lifts. Dame Aylin, the Nightsong — Selûne's immortal daughter — was imprisoned there.

The gods of the Realms in play: Selûne (moon) and her sister Shar (loss/dark); Mystra (magic, Gale's patron); Tyr (justice) and Ilmater (endurance); Tymora (luck) and Gond (invention); Withers serves Jergal, scribe of the dead.

Avernus & the Hells: the first layer of the Nine Hells, ruled by the archdevil Zariel. Wyll is bound by a pact to the cambion Mizora; Karlach's heart is an infernal engine forged there; Elturel was dragged there and back.
The githyanki: Lae'zel's people, ruled from the Astral Plane by the lich-queen Vlaakith; their red-dragon-riding patrols hunt illithids across the planes and resent the living.

Mind flayers & Elder Brains: illithids of the Underdark breed by ceremorphosis (a tadpole consuming a host's brain); an enslaved Elder Brain became the Netherbrain. Free tadpoles and a stray illithid or two remain at large.

Notable Lower City landmarks: the Elfsong Tavern (haunted by a singing elf-ghost), Sorcerous Sundries (the great magic-shop), the Blushing Mermaid and the Low Lantern (dockside dens), Baldur's Mouth (the city gazette), and the temples of the Lower City.
Notable Upper City landmarks: Wyrm's Rock fortress (and the wrecked Steel Watch foundry below it), the High Hall and the Counting House, and the patriars' estates behind the Basilisk Gate.

The Sword Coast around the Gate: the river Chionthar runs to the sea; Wyrm's Crossing and the Risen Road lead north toward Elturel, Scornubel, and Berdusk; Candlekeep's library stands to the south; Waterdeep lies far up the coast.

The tadpole-touched: thousands carried Absolute tadpoles; some were cured, some were not, a few gained strange powers. A reactionary movement wants them registered, exiled, or worse — the war's living wound.
standing_threads: The power vacuum: with Gortash dead and the Steel Watch gone, the patriars, the Flaming Fist, the Guild, and the Zhentarim all maneuver for control of the Gate — quietly, and not always quietly.
Loose ends of the Absolute: scattered cult remnants, freed illithids, and the lingering, ambiguous influence of the Emperor — the mind flayer that helped save the city and serves only itself.
The fear of the tadpole-touched: thousands were infected and cured (or not); a reactionary movement wants them registered, exiled, or worse.

regions.name: Baldur's Gate — Lower City
regions.description: The beating, crowded heart inside the old walls: the Elfsong Tavern, the Baldur's Mouth gazette, temples to Tymora and Gond, merchant rows, and the raw scar in the streets where the Netherbrain breached. Refugees and tadpole-survivors crowd the alleys. The default hub.

regions.name: Baldur's Gate — Upper City
regions.description: Behind the Basilisk Gate: the patriars' marble district, the High Hall, the Counting House, and Wyrm's Rock fortress with the wrecked Steel Watch foundry below it. Old money, old families, and a vacant Archduke's seat everyone is circling.

regions.name: The Outer City & Rivington
regions.description: The sprawl outside the walls — Rivington's circus-grounds and shrines, the Sharess's Caress, smugglers' docks, and the desperate who can't afford to live inside. Where the Guild and the Zhentarim do their real business.

regions.name: Wyrm's Crossing & the Risen Road
regions.description: The fortified toll-bridges over the Chionthar and the road north — Flaming Fist checkpoints, caravans, banditry, and the long road to Elturel and beyond. The Gate's front door to the Sword Coast.

regions.name: Elturel
regions.description: The city that went to Avernus and came back. Its people carry the hells behind their eyes; the Hellriders patrol a town rebuilding its faith under an empty sky where the Companion once burned. Devils still take an interest.

regions.name: Reithwin & the Lifting Shadow
regions.description: The Shadow-Cursed Lands around Moonrise Towers, where Ketheric Thorm's curse of Shar is slowly lifting since his fall — Last Light Inn rekindles, the dead grow quieter, and survivors return to a poisoned country to see what crawled out of the dark.

regions.name: Candlekeep
regions.description: The great fortress-library on the Sword Coast, hoarding the world's knowledge behind a one-book toll. If the truth about the Crown of Karsus, the Emperor's past, or a loose illithid is written anywhere, it is here — guarded by Avowed who do not love visitors.

factions.name: The Flaming Fist
factions.description: The Gate's mercenary army and de facto police, overstretched and leaderless-feeling with the Steel Watch gone and the dukedom contested. Honorable in the ranks, political at the top.

factions.name: The Guild
factions.description: Baldur's Gate's vast thieves' network — smuggling, protection, information. Pragmatic, everywhere, and the ones who actually know what moves in the dark.

factions.name: The Zhentarim (Black Network)
factions.description: The mercantile-mercenary cabal filling the power vacuum with coin, blades, and contracts. Smiling, ruthless, expansionist.

factions.name: The Harpers
factions.description: The covert network that fights tyranny and unchecked power — battered from the Absolute war but watching the vacuum closely. Idealists with knives.

factions.name: Remnants of the Absolute
factions.description: Scattered cultists, abandoned true souls, and freed illithids who still hear an echo of the brain. The world's lingering antagonist gravity — broken, desperate, and dangerous precisely because they have nothing left.

npc_roster.name: Jaheira
npc_roster.role: High Harper, veteran of a hundred years
npc_roster.personality: A half-elf druid-warrior and Harper leader who has buried more friends than most people meet. Dry, fierce, maternal in a way that bites; she has saved the Coast before and is too tired and too stubborn to stop now. The player's likeliest mentor and door into the Harpers.
npc_roster.hook: Suspects someone is gathering the Absolute's loose ends — and that the new powers circling the dukedom are not all what they claim.

npc_roster.name: Minsc and Boo
npc_roster.role: ranger of legend (and his miniature giant space hamster) — candidate COMPANION
npc_roster.personality: Booming, bighearted, gloriously simple-seeming and far shrewder than he sounds; speaks to and for Boo, the 'miniature giant space hamster.' A hero of ages past, lately unfrozen and itching to 'go for the eyes.' Loyal unto death; grieves the friends time took from him.
npc_roster.hook: Available as a companion; his old griefs (Dynaheir, the centuries he lost) surface whenever loss or duty is in play.

npc_roster.name: Astarion
npc_roster.role: freed vampire spawn, now his own master
npc_roster.personality: A high-elf rogue of razor wit and centuries of cruelty survived; charming, vain, wounded under the glamour. Two hundred years a slave to the vampire Cazador — now free, recalibrating what a person without a master even wants. Self-interest worn like couture, with unexpected loyalty beneath.
npc_roster.hook: Hunts the last of Cazador's old network in the Outer City — and the other spawn he left behind in the dark.

npc_roster.name: Shadowheart
npc_roster.role: cleric at a crossroads of Shar and Selûne
npc_roster.personality: A half-elf cleric whose memories were stolen and whose faith — to Shar, goddess of loss and the dark, or to Selûne, the moon — is the wound at her center. Guarded, sharp, capable of devotion or ruin. Carries the weight of choices the war forced on her.
npc_roster.hook: What she did with the Nightsong, and whether her parents live, still shapes who comes looking for her.

npc_roster.name: Wyll Ravengard
npc_roster.role: the Blade of Frontiers, a Duke's son
npc_roster.personality: A warlock hero, theatrical and genuinely noble, who paid for his heroics with a pact and a price. Son of Duke Ulder Ravengard. Wants to do right and keeps discovering what right costs.
npc_roster.hook: Torn between the city's empty seat (his father's legacy) and the road — and a devil's contract that is never quite settled.

npc_roster.name: Karlach
npc_roster.role: tiefling barbarian with an infernal engine
npc_roster.personality: All open-hearted fury and warmth — a tiefling whose heart is a roaring infernal engine that is killing her, sold to Avernus by Gortash years ago. Lives loud because she may not live long. The most alive person in any room.
npc_roster.hook: Her engine, and whether Avernus or a Gate artificer can mend it, is a clock over her head — and a reason to hate what Gortash built.

npc_roster.name: The Emperor
npc_roster.role: mind flayer — ambiguous power, possible antagonist
npc_roster.personality: A mind flayer of immense intellect and older identity, who helped end the Absolute and serves, finally, only itself. Reasonable, seductive, utterly without sentiment. It does not lie so much as choose which truths to feed you. The most dangerous 'ally' on the Coast.
npc_roster.hook: Moves unseen in the city's underbelly; its goals are its own, and they are not finished.

npc_roster.name: Withers
npc_roster.role: the undying keeper of the dead
npc_roster.personality: A gaunt, ancient revenant of few words and dust-dry humor who keeps a ledger of souls and turns up where death has been busy. Knows far more than he says about gods, fate, and the war just ended. Neutral as the grave.
npc_roster.hook: Appears at thresholds of death and choice; offers the player cryptic perspective and, occasionally, a second chance.

story_seeds: The contested dukedom: someone must take Gortash's empty seat, and the patriars, the Fist, the Zhentarim, and the Guild are all maneuvering — by ballot, blade, or blackmail (the slow main thread).
Loose ends of the Absolute: a cult remnant or a freed illithid surfaces, still echoing the brain, gathering the desperate.
The tadpole question: a reactionary patriar pushes to register and exile the tadpole-survivors; a survivor the party knows is on the list.
Elturel's debt: a devil comes to the Gate to collect on a soul-bargain made when the city hung over Avernus.
Cazador's leavings: vampire spawn abandoned in the Outer City, leaderless and starving, draw the Gur hunters and the Guild into a quiet war.
Candlekeep's secret: a page the Avowed won't sell holds the truth about the Crown of Karsus — or about the Emperor's first name.

quest_variants.name: The Fate of the Emerald Grove

outcomes.lore: The druid grove in the Western wilds still stands; the goblin warband that besieged it was broken and the tiefling refugees sheltering there lived to walk the road to the city. Grateful druids tend a sanctuary that held.
outcomes.hook: A druid who survived the siege now travels the Risen Road looking for the scattered refugees they once sheltered — and would pay for word of where the survivors settled.

outcomes.lore: The grove fell. The warband poured through the gate and the refugees were slaughtered among the standing stones; the place is a burned shrine no one tends, its carvings black with old fire.
outcomes.hook: A lone tiefling who crawled out of the grove's ashes has been seen in the Outer City, nursing a grudge and asking after anyone who profited from the massacre.

outcomes.lore: The shadow-touched faction among the druids won the grove's inner quarrel: the refugees were driven out unprotected and most never reached safety. The circle sealed itself off, turned inward, and admits no outsider now.
outcomes.hook: The sealed grove has stopped answering the rangers who used to trade with it; a worried warden wants someone to learn what the isolationist druids are hiding behind their thorns.

quest_variants.name: The State of the Shadow-Cursed Lands

outcomes.lore: The Shadow Curse over Reithwin is breaking. Green creeps back across poisoned ground, the dead grow quiet, and a great healer has stayed behind to shepherd the land's slow recovery and the orphans resettling there.
outcomes.hook: The healing land keeps turning up things the curse had swallowed — a buried hamlet, a sealed crypt, a name on a gravestone someone in the city has been searching for. The warden of Reithwin needs hands he can trust.

outcomes.lore: The curse never lifted. Reithwin and the lands around Moonrise stay drowned in unnatural dark; the things that hunt there still hunt, and a single grim warden holds a line that cannot be won, only held.
outcomes.hook: The lone warden of the cursed lands has gone silent. The last traveler back from the dark says his lantern still burns at Last Light — but no one answers the door.

outcomes.lore: The dark was contained but not cured: the Flaming Fist threw a cordon around the Shadow-Cursed Lands and call it a quarantine. Smugglers run the line, deserters hide past it, and the curse waits behind the wire.
outcomes.hook: Something valuable was left behind the quarantine line when it went up, and more than one party is quietly hiring runners willing to cross into the dark to fetch it.

outcomes.lore: The empty Archduke's seat sits under the restored Council of Four, who govern a grieving, rebuilding city by uneasy committee. No one tyrant holds the Gate; the patriars, the Fist, and the Guild jockey within the law, mostly.
outcomes.hook: A council vote on the vacant Archduke's seat is coming, and every faction in the city wants a deniable pair of hands to tilt it. Someone has already approached the newcomer.

outcomes.lore: The Archduke holds the Gate with an iron fist and a rebuilt watch of arcane constructs. The streets are orderly and afraid; dissent disappears quietly into the cells beneath Wyrm's Rock. Order, bought at the price of the city's throat.
outcomes.hook: A resistance cell needs someone with no record and no face the watch knows to carry a message past the construct patrols into the Upper City.

outcomes.lore: No council sits in judgment but one. A crowned Chosen of Bhaal rules the Gate's terrorized nights from a seat slick with the city's blood, and its powers kneel, flee, or feed the altar. The Archduke's seat is filled at last - by the one thing no one prayed for.
outcomes.hook: What's left of the resistance is a handful of names whispered in cellars; they need a face the murder-court has never seen to carry word between the cells still drawing breath.

outcomes.lore: The Council of Four still convenes, still votes, still believes it governs the Gate. It does not. An unseen illithid power holds the true reins from below, and every debate lands the way it has already decided. The seat is occupied - by something no patriar can see to name.
outcomes.hook: Someone noticed the votes never break the way the arguments should. They want a nobody to trace the strings to whatever hand is pulling them - and to live to report back.

outcomes.lore: The seat stays empty and the city tears quietly at itself over it: the patriars, the Flaming Fist, the Guild, and the Zhentarim all maneuver for the throne by ballot, blade, and blackmail, and no one has won.
outcomes.hook: Two factions both think they've hired the newcomer to do the same job for opposite ends — and only one of them can be paid.

quest_variants.name: The Steel Watch and the Gnome Factions

outcomes.lore: The war-construct foundry beneath Wyrm's Rock lies wrecked, its automatons dead in the streets — but the enslaved artificer-smiths who were forced to build them walked free, and their craft hall is reopening in the Lower City under their own god's mark.
outcomes.hook: The freed smiths are buying back their dead constructs' control-cores at any price — and someone has started murdering the scavengers who hold them.

outcomes.lore: The foundry is wrecked and the constructs are scrap, but it was the gnome resistance-fighters who came out of the rubble alive while their rival smiths did not. Their leader walks the Lower City as a triumphant, vengeful liberator.
outcomes.hook: The surviving gnome faction is hunting down everyone who collaborated with the construct-foundry — and the lists they're working from are not always right about who was guilty.

outcomes.lore: Against all odds both gnome factions came out of the foundry's fall alive, brokered into an uneasy peace under a single reluctant leader. The dead Steel Watch hulks they pick apart together are the only thing they agree on.
outcomes.hook: The fragile gnome peace is one incident away from a feud, and someone is staging incidents. A peace-broker wants the provocateur found before the streets run with it.

outcomes.lore: The murder-god's cult did not merely survive — it triumphed, and rules the city's nights from a temple of blood beneath the streets. The killings are no longer hidden; they are tithes, and the city has learned not to be out after dark.
outcomes.hook: A grieving family will pay everything they have left for someone to walk into the abattoir under the city and bring back a body the cult took — or proof of who marked them for the knife.

outcomes.lore: The Bhaalist cult was gutted: its shapeshifting matriarch dead, its temple-tribunal cleared, the murder-shrines cold. What's left are cold cases — the unsolved temple killings of the war years — and a hollyphant investigator still closing the files.
outcomes.hook: An old murder the broken cult never finished has reopened: the same ritual marks, a copycat or a survivor, and the investigator working it has gone missing.

outcomes.lore: The cult was driven underground but never broken. Bhaalist murder-shrines still fester in the city's underbelly and the killings have started again — quieter, patient, recruiting from the desperate the war left behind.
outcomes.hook: A string of ritual killings shares one detail the Flaming Fist won't make public, and a frightened watch sergeant is hiring outside help because he no longer knows who in his own house to trust.

outcomes.lore: The tiefling refugees who fled the western wilds reached the Gate and made it theirs: a community took root in Rivington, its survivors — a disgraced leader, an orphan-turned-operator, a gifted young smith — woven into the city's recovering life.
outcomes.hook: The refugee community is being squeezed out of the homes it built by a patriar's land claim, and its leaders are looking for someone willing to dig up why a noble suddenly wants their corner of Rivington.

outcomes.lore: Few of the refugees ever reached the Gate, and those who did scattered into its underside rather than a community — a thief in the Guild's debt, a beggar in the sewers, names that drift through the Outer City and don't stay anywhere long.
outcomes.hook: One of the scattered refugees has surfaced with a story about who really doomed the others on the road — and is being hunted for telling it.

outcomes.lore: The survivors made it, but bitter: a hard knot of refugees in the Outer City who trust no one outside their own and remember exactly who turned them away at the gates when they arrived starving. The city calls them a problem; they call it surviving.
outcomes.hook: The bitter refugee enclave has taken to answering the city's contempt in kind, and a relief worker who still believes in them needs an outsider they might actually listen to.

outcomes.lore: The imprisoned immortal — the moon-goddess's own daughter, caged for a hundred years under the Shadow-Cursed Lands — walks free. Last Light held; the covert network that sheltered there survived; a living icon of the moon faith stands again in the world.
outcomes.hook: The freed immortal is hunting the last of her old jailers, and her crusade has led her to the Gate — where she needs mortal hands to do the quiet work a legend cannot.

outcomes.lore: The cage was never opened; the imprisoned immortal was lost when the refuge at Last Light fell, and the network that sheltered there died with it. There is a goddess-shaped absence in the world's history and a massacre site no one will name.
outcomes.hook: A relic looted from the fallen refuge at Last Light has surfaced in a Gate market, and the survivors of that network — what few there are — want it back badly enough to pay or to kill.

No in-game text is reproduced; outcomes STATE facts in our own words, like the ending overlays.

starting_options.framing: Default. The player arrives in the recovering Lower City — newcomers, hired blades, or survivors of the tadpole crisis — and is pulled into a thread.
The player comes up the Risen Road into the Gate's front door, past Flaming Fist checkpoints and the desperate.
The player returns to the lifting Shadow-Cursed Lands to see what the curse left behind — grimmer, more personal.

dm_guidance: Run this as a LIVING SANDBOX in the immediate aftermath of Baldur's Gate 3, NOT a replay of it. On start_world: seed the regions, factions, and history/standing-threads into memory (recall keeps the city consistent). Drop the party at a starting_option, then GENERATE the specific scene/NPC on arrival and PERSIST it (add_location/create_character/remember/add_quest) so the city grows and is carried across sessions. The BG3 companions in the roster are living LEGENDS now — pull them in as allies, patrons, complications, or a recruited companion (Minsc is ready), but they have their own lives; don't make the story about them. Let the standing threads (the dukedom, the Absolute's remnants, the tadpole fear) move whether or not the party is watching. Stage morally-grey antagonists warmth-first. Hold the dungeon-master skill's craft bar: felt menace, a wounded companion, show-don't-tell, the unforgettable beat. GRANDEUR is the hardest dimension here — don't let a session live in one tavern: move the party through at least two locations, and make the post-Absolute scale PRESS ON THE ROOM as physical things, not lore recited — a Steel Watch relic sold for parts with its eye still faintly lit, cobblestones still warm over a Wound that should be cold, a driftglobe that flickers when the Emperor is named, a Flaming Fist checkpoint that wasn't on this corner yesterday. Mature themes, handled with weight — this is the Baldur's Gate register.
